newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Seeking basis for upside move.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK - Seeking basis for upside move.

text.p: The U.S. credit market will sort through a morass of indicators on Thursday in an effort reestablish the positive momentum it has lacked so far this week.

Market analysts said cheaper Treasuries may begin to look like bargains again after prices slipped on Wednesday as weak European markets, supply jitters and talk of foreign central bank sales overshadowed a reassuring consumer price report,

If all of Thursday's reports come in according to estimates, they would all represent month-over-month or week-over-week declines, suggesting the market certainly has potential for a move to the upside.
"The market can certainly do better depending on what kind of stimulus Thursday's catalysts furnish," said Matthew Alexy, chief market strategist at CS First Boston.
The data bombardment will start at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT when jobless claims data for the week ended October 12 hit the tape alongside September housing starts figures.
Economists surveyed by Reuters predicted jobless claims would show a signficant rise to 331,000 after a surprisingly hefty drop to 319,000 last week.
Housing starts are expected to drop to 1.47 million annualized units in September from 1.525 million in the previous month.

"You had a very outsized decline in claims last week and it will be very important to see if you get a rise this week," said Cheryl Katz, senior economist at Merrill Lynch, noting that the Columbus Day holiday could skew the numbers.
"Housing starts will also be important," she added. "We keep looking for a slowdown and we better start seeing it."

Shortly after the housing and claims data, September industrial production and capacity utilization figures will be released, followed by the October Philadelphia Federal Reserve Bank's manufacturing survey and August inventories numbers at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.

Based on weak manufacturing sector data in the recent employment report, economists are expecting a meager 0.1 percent gain in industrial production for September versus a 0.5 percent gain in the previous month.
Capacity utilization is seen edging down to 83.3 from 83.5 percent.
Business inventories for August are seen rising 0.3 percent, but analysts said the Philly Fed survey, which represents fourth quarter data, could steal the spotlight.

"A lot of (Thursday's) information is the kind of stuff that allows forecasters to round out their (third quarter) GDP expectations," said Alexy. "Traders are much more concerned about whether you're seeing a pickup into the fourth quarter."
Economists expect the headline Philly Fed index to come in at 11.9 versus 13.9 in September.

The benchmark 6.75 percent 30-year bond was off 5/32 at 98-21/32 to yield 6.86 percent in late Wednesday trade. The federal funds rate is expected to open between 5-3/16 and 5-1/4 percent on Thursday.
